A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 21-page versions of Multiplayer Nash Preference Optimization. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that the scientific text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–G support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original MNPO experiments on instruction-following, knowledge, reasoning, and coding benchmarks in Tables 2–4, with additional ablations and repeated-run results in Tables 5–8.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experimental results in Tables 2–8, including the main benchmark evaluations and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The MNPO objectives, TD-MNPO and HT-MNPO procedures, Algorithms 1–2, and external-opponent formulation in Appendix G.1 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same UltraFeedback-based training data, instruction-following benchmarks, eleven academic benchmarks, and homogeneous and heterogeneous preference scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every reported comparison, including SFT, DPO, SimPO, SPPO, INPO, and the additional open- and closed-source models in Table 2.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix C retain the same model configurations, three-iteration training procedure, data splits, metrics, and judge settings. The appendix evaluation protocols also match.

E4.justification: Tables 5–8 retain the same analyses of player count, alternative base model, evaluator variation, and two-player versus three-player HT-MNPO. No ablation or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Table 7 reports the same means and standard deviations across three runs under the same three LLM judges. No run-count or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and reported findings are unchanged. For example, Table 2 retains TD-MNPO scores of 57.27 on AlpacaEval 2.0, 52.26 on Arena-Hard, and 7.03 on MT-Bench; appendix results also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, update derivations, Lemma 1, and Propositions 1–2 are unchanged, including the proofs and analysis in Appendices F and G.1.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about multiplayer generalization, homogeneous convergence guarantees, unification of existing methods, and empirical benefits.

C2.justification: Results interpretations and applicability discussions are unchanged. Appendix G retains the same limitations concerning oracle quality, diminishing informativeness of binary preferences, and absent convergence guarantees for heterogeneous oracles.

D1.justification: Appendix C retains identical hardware, hyperparameters, data-processing instructions, implementation sources, and evaluation configuration. Code and data access information is unchanged; the added funding attribution supplies no technical reproducibility details.

R1.justification: Section 6, Appendix A, and the cited works are unchanged. Bibliography entries that move between pages remain present with identical content.

P1.justification: v4 appends fuller IITP/MSIT funding attribution for the already acknowledged grant on page 11 and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. Scientific prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The expanded acknowledgment shifts the reference-list layout and moves existing entries across page breaks on pages 11–15. Figure 1, Tables 1–9, and appendix layouts are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 provides fuller attribution for the existing funding acknowledgment, but the scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information, and limitations remain identical. This administrative addition and the resulting bibliography reflow do not meaningfully change overall paper quality.
